rich_summary: Victor Frankenstein throws himself obsessively into natural philosophy at Ingolstadt, guided by the contrasting professors Krempe and Waldman. His fascination narrows toward the ultimate mystery: the origin of life. To understand it, he studies anatomy and the decay of bodies, haunting vaults and charnel-houses until a breakthrough arrives—he discovers the secret of generating life and animating lifeless matter. Rather than revealing the method, Victor warns that such knowledge brings ruin. Consumed by ambition, he decides to construct a human being, enlarging the design to a gigantic eight-foot form for practical reasons. Working alone in a hidden workshop, gathering bones and materials from dissecting rooms and slaughterhouses, he becomes physically and mentally degraded. Nature, family, and morality fade as his feverish labor drives him toward completing his creation.

highlight_spans.why: Victor turns from abstract science to the forbidden boundary between life and death, marking the thematic pivot toward creation.
The moment Victor claims he has discovered the cause of life and the power to animate lifeless matter—the central breakthrough of the novel.
Victor imagines the glory of creating a new species that would bless him as its creator, revealing the hubris driving his experiment.
The gruesome description of graveyards, bones, and secret labor captures the eerie horror and moral decay surrounding the creature’s construction.
Victor’s physical collapse—fever, nerves, and isolation—shows the psychological toll of his obsession as the creation nears completion.

top_scenes.scene_text: Victor alone at midnight in a cramped attic laboratory, moonlight through a window illuminating bones, dissecting tools, and a massive unfinished humanoid frame on the table.
Victor wandering among open graves and charnel-house vaults with a lantern, studying decaying bodies while shadows loom over the damp stone walls.
In feverish obsession, Victor assembles gigantic limbs and sinews in his hidden workshop while summer sunlight glows outside, ignored.
